newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Greece and EU partners in stand-off over Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Greece and EU partners in stand-off over Cyprus.

text.p: Greece and its European Union partners were locked in a stand-off on Monday over whether the northern Turkish third of Cyprus should be involved in the process of admitting the island to the bloc.
Athens was holding out against a push by the other 14 members away from a previous policy that Cyprus's membership could be limited to its southern Greek part.
"We are aiming at an agreement with the whole of Cyprus," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told a news conference.
"We have not reached a consensus on the precise draft of the EU's position, and we will be meeting again this afternoon to discuss this," he said.
"Both sides have to be involved at some stage. When that happens, how that happens is what we are working on," British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind told a news conference.

The failure to agree on a position would mean that although foreign ministers from the Union and Cyprus could hold a planned association council meeting on Tuesday, they would not be able to use it to prepare future entry talks.
Talks are scheduled to start six months after the EU concludes its ongoing intergovernmental review of its workings.

Diplomats said that the strong stance by Greece's 14 EU partners was designed to pressure Athens to negotiate a settlement to the divided island, of which Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974, in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia that was backed by Athens.
The international community, with the exception of Turkey, recognises the Greek Cypriot adminstration as the island's only government.
